claim: R2-08: "The volume test is the home of which base-bar clauses it runs: its head names each bar it takes …, and a lettered clause re-running one names it. Scope's take-over table carries the same ids in its base-bar column." The table (base l. 18220–18231) and §13.2's groups' runs lists miss ids the live tests name: (a) the calibration row (l. 18230) lists ids for items 120–126 only, while T-V12-44 names T111-1 – T111-5, T-V12-45 T112-1, T-V12-46 T113-2 (and T113-5's milestone), T-V12-47 T114-4 – T114-7, T-V12-48 takes T115-1, T115-4 and T116-1, T-V12-49 names T117-2 and T118-2 – T118-6, and T-V12-50 takes T119-1, T119-2, T119-4 and T119-5; (b) the stage-3 row (l. 18224) gives T-V2-58 "T115-1's composed shapes" only, while its (f) registers B-MASS on the rung pin "(V12 §2.13; T115-4)", and T-V2-59 "T123-5" only, while its (d) runs "T123-7's no-op"; (c) the plan-rung row (l. 18223) gives T-V3-37 "T119-2's plan clauses", while its clauses run T119-2, T119-3, T119-4 and T119-5, and T-V3-40 the plan clauses of T122-1 – T122-3, while its (f) runs "V12's `item122.crises` pin (V12 §2.13; T122-7)"; (d) the evolution row (l. 18220) has no T114-10, though §13.8 runs T114-10's 10 epochs "with M6-E's E3" and T-V6-73's welded-stretch clause runs them (VAP-r2-04); (e) the SettlementForge row (l. 18227) gives T-V8-62 "T126-2's host-frame clause" only, while it runs "V09's T126-3 scan … over `embed.html`"; (f) the application row (l. 18229) names no item-112 bar, while T-V9-72 runs T112-1's style check on the thematic views and T112-2's trial. §13.2's groups (the third statement of the same assignment) also diverge: item 111's runs list (l. 18010–18011) names no test and omits volume 8 (T-V8-50, the port's clauses); item 112's (l. 18012–18018) has none; item 113's (l. 18028–18029) names no test and omits volume 7 (T-V7-59, the village halves of T113-1 and T113-3); items 114, 115, 119, 122, 123 and 126's lists omit (b)–(e)'s clauses.
required_change: In §13.2's take-over table: the calibration row's base-bar column reads "every bar's register line and its spec, the specs, pins and bench bars of items 111–126: T111-1 – T111-5 (T-V12-44); T112-1's style line (T-V12-45); T113-2 and T113-5's registration (T-V12-46); T114-4 – T114-7 (T-V12-47); T115-1, T115-4 and T116-1 (T-V12-48); T117-2 and T118-2 – T118-6 (T-V12-49); T119-1, T119-2, T119-4 and T119-5 (T-V12-50); T120-1 and T120-6 (T-V12-52); …" (the rest as it stands); the stage-3 row reads "T115-1's composed shapes and T115-4's rung clause on B-MASS (T-V2-58), …, T123-5 and T123-7's exterior clause (T-V2-59)"; the plan-rung row "T119-2 – T119-5's plan clauses (T-V3-37), …, T122-1's, T122-2's, T122-3's and T122-7's plan clauses (T-V3-40)"; the evolution row adds "T114-10's epoch clause (T-V6-73)"; the SettlementForge row "T126-2's host-frame clause and T126-3's embed clause (T-V8-62)"; the application row adds "T112-1's thematic-view clause and T112-2 (T-V9-72)". In §13.2's groups: item 111's runs list reads "Volume 7 runs them at the village rungs (T-V7-58), volume 6 over epochs, a failing spring weakening its pull (T-V6-72), volume 8 the port's clauses (T-V8-50) and volume 12 the specs, the pin and the register lines (T-V12-44)"; item 112's gains "Volume 9 runs T112-1 on its thematic views and T112-2's trial (T-V9-72) and volume 12 the style line (T-V12-45)"; item 113's reads "Volume 6 runs them on its replay engine (T-V6-71), volume 4 T113-4 and T113-5 on the underground's output (T-V4-77, T-V4-76), volume 7 the village halves of T113-1 and T113-3 (T-V7-59), volume 8 the dossier's history (T-V8-51), volume 12 their register lines and the replay's budget (T-V12-46)"; item 114's "Volume 6 runs T114-1 – T114-5, T114-8's and T114-10's epoch clauses on its engine (T-V6-73)"; item 115's "volume 2 on composed shapes and the rung pin on B-MASS (T-V2-58)"; item 119's "volume 3 the plan's (T-V3-37: T119-2 – T119-5)"; item 122's "volume 3 the plan clauses of T122-1 – T122-3 and T122-7 (T-V3-40)"; item 123's "volume 2 T123-5 and T123-7's exterior clause (T-V2-59)"; item 126's "volume 8 T126-2's host-frame clause and T126-3's embed clause (T-V8-62)". (The volume ends are VAP-r2-02 – VAP-r2-06.)

claim: §13.8 (l. 18840) schedules "T126-1 – T126-3 | PR on volume 9's app harness | M2a (with the medium layout)", and T126-1 requires that "at the medium class every tool of V09 §4.12's list completes its canvas script under touch". At M2a only T9 `shape` and T10 `hold` exist (V09 AP2; T2 `ground` – T8 `fill` land at M3a, AP3). The takers place it otherwise: T-V9-22's milestone "M2a (T126-2, T126-3); M3a (every tool's touch script)", T-V12-59 "M2a (§16); each tool's script from the milestone that lands it, every tool from M3a", V12 §3.15.16 "each tool from the milestone that lands it, every tool from M3a". By §13.2's convention (2) a bar runs "from the milestone §13.8's schedule gives it", so the base gates every tool's touch script at M2a, which the volumes do not.
required_change: §13.8's row reads "| T126-1 – T126-3 | PR on volume 9's app harness | M2a (with the medium layout); T126-1 each tool from the milestone that lands it, every tool from M3a |".

claim: Item 116's export bar at the METROPOLIS cap has two outcomes. §13.2's T116-4 (base l.18077–18078) now reads 'every export frames within the limit, the whole bounds at most, or stop 0's extent where the bounds are wider than the window at stop 0'. R2-30's clause describes a view; an export has no window (§11.2's export runs in the worker and in Node with no viewport), and §8.7, the export frame's home (l.13879–13882), cuts every export only to the limit bounds ('the whole limit bounds at most … a requested frame reaching past them is cut to them'), window-free, as item 116 (c) says ('EXPORTS frame within the same limit (the whole bounds at most)'). At the cap the bar either fails §8.7's whole-map export (a print of the 17.53 km frame cut to a window's stop-0 extent) or cannot be evaluated headless.
required_change: T116-4 reads: 'every export frames within the limit bounds (§8.7: the whole bounds — town and camps while a crisis look stands — at most), at any window size and with none; at the METROPOLIS cap a whole-bounds PNG, print and SVG export frames the whole bounds'. R2-30's 'or stop 0 where the bounds are wider than the window at stop 0' stays in T116-1's view bar only.

claim: No bar exercises VKr2-01's case: a raised way whose deck ends on the outer ring, carried through an epoch's frame growth. T110-2 (§13.2, l. 17982–17985) builds 'its part sized to the ground's frame plus margin and growing with it' and 'an aqueduct sourced beyond the frame laid to the outer ring without a ramp' as separate clauses. §13.1's kernel set (l. 17186–17190) grows a frame only in 'a frame growth whose frame and arena would be no larger' and 'a village → town fold'. Nothing checks the foot through the growth: it must resolve at every stage end, the old ground vertex must leave nothing behind, and both ends must lie on the new rings after §4.11. Under principle (11) an untested edge is a major.
required_change: §13.2 T110-2: after 'an aqueduct sourced beyond the frame laid to the outer ring without a ramp,' add 'and the same aqueduct through an epoch's frame growth — §3.10's stored-references row passing at every stage end of the epoch, no part-0 vertex left with a row and no edge, and after §4.11 both ends of its ring-end foot on the new rings (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`, §3.2 (9)) —'.

One price, two statements.
required_change: J-A120.01's index row ends "— built at M5 with volume 1's area and gap services, its base parts priced by absorption into the O11 and O12 lines (its overlay provider and panel volume 9's AP11; J-A568.05)".
